newsitem.title: CANADA: Barrick says now world's 2nd biggest gold producer.
newsitem.headline: Barrick says now world's 2nd biggest gold producer.

text.p: (All figures U.S. dollars unless otherwise noted)
Canada's Barrick Gold Corp. said on Wednesday it had supplanted Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd. to become the world's second largest gold producer.
Barrick's 1996 gold production was 3,148,801 ounces, surpassing Gold Fields' 3,125,631 ounces for fiscal 1996.
Barrick expects 1997 production again to top three million ounces.

The Toronto-based company posted a 40 percent increase in its proven and probable reserves to 51 million ounces from 36.5 million ounces a year earlier. It also reported 25 million ounces of gold in the resource category -- a gold find not yet fully proven.
Barrick reported its fourth-quarter and full-year profits fell, due mainly to higher operating and exploration costs.
Fourth-quarter earnings declined to $56 million, or 15 cents a share, from a year-earlier $78 million, or 22 cents a share.
Earnings for the full year dipped to $218 million, or 60 cents a share, from $292 million, or 82 cents a share in 1995.
Barrick makes no secret of its ambition to become the world's largest gold company, surpassing Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd., which in 1996 produced about seven million ounces of gold.
To clinch first place, Barrick is now seeking control of the huge Busang deposit in Indonesia, said to be one of this century's most sensational gold discoveries.
Barrick has been negotiating with Calgary, Alberta-based Bre-X Minerals Ltd. for months to control the discovery, but its chances of success are up in the air.

"One of the messages they'll probably try to get across is that they (Barrick) are not desperate for it, they certainly don't need it, they have an awful lot already," said gold analyst Catherine Gignac at Deacon Capital in Toronto.
Barrick's shares were down C40 cents to C$35.70 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Wednesday and by 37.5 cents to $26.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
